Masala is basically a blend of spices but it varies from home to home in India. The Major Indian cuisines we represent are: Kashmir: The crown of India, the cuisine is influenced by the Muslims and Hindus, rice and vegetables, saffron and spices, mild on heat and great fruity flavors Delhi: Capital of India, Haute cuisine of India influenced by the Mughal emperors. In Delhi, food has the same value of the deities and there are even streets named after the age old famous restaurants handed down from generation to generation. Rajasthan: The Sahara of India has raised the finest warriors and the cuisine is influenced by the scarcity of fresh produce and the long journeys that a warrior has to undertake during their hunting expeditions. Punjab: “Granary of India” or “Bread basket of India” “Land of Five Rivers”, Punjab is known by many names. It’s better known for its festivities, the colorful food and the Tandoor clay oven. Punjabi folks are true to their heart and so is their cuisine!! Goa: “The party people of India!!!” The cuisine is heavily influenced by the Portuguese, the Catholics and the Hindus. The cuisine features pork, chili, seafood, coconuts & vinegar. Chennai: Formerly known as “Madras”, capital of Tamil Nadu. Folks here believe in serving food as a humanity service and takes great care in it. Traces of Tamilian cuisine can be seen in Sri Lanka, Malaysia, and Singapore due to the migration of the Tamilians. Rice and rice flour dishes are more dominant in this cuisine. Kerala: “Land of Spices” since 3000BC, is a state of greenery where everything grows in abundance especially the coconuts and brown rice. The food unites the Keralite irrespective of their caste, politics, color or religion. The cuisine features rice, rice flour, spices, ginger, beef, duck, pork, seafood, back water fish, lagoon crustaceans, coconuts, tamarind, and many more. Every religion and every district has their own handwritten age old recipes which is passed from generation to generation with great passion. Indo Chinese: Indian-Chinese cuisine originated in India and is a uniquely South Asian Phenomenon. Towards the end of nineteenth and start of the twentieth century, Hakka-speaking Chinese immigrated to the eastern Indian city of Kolkata (formerly known as Calcutta) to work in tanneries, ports, and railways and soon established the country’s only Chinatown. As Chinese ingredients were manipulated to suit the spicy, fried food-craving palates of Indians, a food fusion took off. We have only slightly scratched the tip of the Indian cuisine iceberg in our menu.
